The licence is as Commons records it. Identified as this saint because: A historical print, not an icon: a Rijksmuseum engraving which Commons describes as 'the conversion of St. Eustace: while hunting (on horseback) he is confronted with a stag bearing a crucifix between its antlers', filed in Category:Saint Eustace. That hunting vision is the life of Eustathius Placidas, the great martyr kept on 20 September with his wife and two sons. Commons describes it: De Heilige Eustachius knielend tussen paard en twee honden voor een hert met in het gewei een crucifix. the conversion of St. Eustace: while hunting (on horseback) he is confronted with a stag bearing a crucifix between its antlers; Eustace is shown kneeling before the stag (that appears on a rock)
